title: A full 2026 federal return, in one step
prompt: In 2026, a married couple filing jointly (0 spouses age 65 or older) has $180,000 of wages, $90,000 of traditional IRA distributions, $0 of long-term capital gains and qualified dividends, and $0 of Social Security benefits. They take the standard deduction and have no credits. What is their total federal income tax including any Net Investment Income Tax, rounded to the nearest dollar?

title: A Roth conversion that also makes Social Security taxable
prompt: In 2026, a single filer (the filer age 65 or older) has $37,000 of traditional IRA distributions, $21,000 of long-term capital gains and qualified dividends, and $28,100 of Social Security benefits, with no wages. They take the standard deduction and have no credits. If they also convert $36,000 from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA in 2026, by how many dollars does their total federal income tax (including any Net Investment Income Tax) go up? Round to the nearest dollar.

title: Retirees inside the new senior-deduction phase-out
prompt: In 2026, a married couple filing jointly (both spouses age 65 or older) has $105,500 of traditional IRA distributions, $0 of long-term capital gains and qualified dividends, and $72,300 of Social Security benefits, with no wages. They take the standard deduction and have no credits. What is their total federal income tax including any Net Investment Income Tax, rounded to the nearest dollar?

title: Spotting Rule 2210 violations in a client email
prompt:
FINRA Rule 2210(d)(1) says retail communications may not contain any false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory or misleading statement or claim, and may not predict or project performance. A representative drafted this email to retail clients about a stock mutual fund:

1. Our analysts project the fund will return 15% next year.
2. CDs are FDIC-insured up to $250,000 per depositor; mutual fund shares are not FDIC-insured.
3. We can meet to review whether this fund fits your goals and time horizon.
4. The fund's expense ratio is 0.65% a year, which is taken out of fund assets.
5. You will earn at least 10% a year in this fund.
6. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

Which numbered sentences violate Rule 2210(d)(1)?
